title: Out Loud: A Sapphic romcom
description: Anna is broke, freshly single, and one bad month away from moving back in with her parents. So when she finds a perfect garage apartment at a price she can almost afford, she signs the lease before she can talk herself out of it. The catch: Emily, her landlord, talks to herself. Constantly. Through walls that are thinner than either of them realized. Anna tells herself she'll tune it out. Instead, she starts listening – to Emily's pep talks and panic spirals, her terrible dates and Tuesday meetings, the way her voice goes quiet on the nights she's convinced she's too much for anyone. It's not eavesdropping if you can't help it. It's not falling for someone if they don't know you're there. It's not a problem until it is. A story about two women, thin walls, and learning to be heard.  if(window.mix_csa){window.mix_csa('[cel_widget_id="tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_2"]', '#CardInstancef7YKQ1so71Jc2UQNI96qjA')('mark', 'bb')} if(window.uet){window.uet('bb','tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_2',{wb: 1})} ._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_icon_core_report__Fs1ah{color:#0f1111;color:var(--aok-sfs-color-page-primary-normal-fg,#0f1111);display:inline-block;-webkit-filter:none;filter:none;-webkit-filter:var(--aok-sfs-effect-mode-dark-color-silhouette-white,none);filter:var(--aok-sfs-effect-mode-dark-color-silhouette-white,none);height:20px;margin-right:4px;width:20px}._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_modal_spinner__3bz5K,._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_popover_inner__3tPIV{padding:20px 24px 0;width:65vw}._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_modal_spinner__3bz5K{height:15vh;margin-top:10vh;text-align:center}._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_no_email_alert__1t6PT{margin-bottom:60px}a[id^=tellAmazonDropdown],a[id^=tellAmazon_][id*=Dropdown]{white-space:norma

title: Out Loud: A Steamy Sapphic College Sports Romance (No Half Hearts)
description: Best friends. College athletes. One contract that was supposed to keep it simple. Jules Navarro returns to Cedar Ridge University for senior year determined to focus on basketball and keep her freshly broken heart under control. Riley Hart—the volleyball captain who lives by schedules, tape, and “captain mode”—has always been Jules’s safest place. Until one kiss turns their friendship into something louder. They draft rules. They make a plan. They even pick one trusted ally. Because in-season, in the spotlight, “private” feels safer than “public.” But Jules isn’t built for half-truths, and Riley’s fear of being seen threatens to bench the best thing either of them has ever wanted. Between preseason pressure, future offers, and a relationship that keeps demanding honesty, Jules and Riley have to decide: keep it contained… or choose each other out loud. title: Out Loud: A Memoir
description: From the most brilliant and audacious choreographer of our time, the exuberant tale of a young dancer’s rise to the pinnacle of the performing arts world, and the triumphs and perils of creating work on his own terms—and staying true to himself Before Mark Morris became “the most successful and influential choreographer alive” ( The New York Times ), he was a six year-old in Seattle cramming his feet into Tupperware glasses so that he could practice walking on pointe. Often the only boy in the dance studio, he was called a sissy, a term he wore like a badge of honor. He was unlike anyone else, deeply gifted and spirited. Moving to New York at nineteen, he arrived to one of the great booms of dance in America. Audiences in 1976 had the luxury of Merce Cunningham’s finest experiments with time and space, of Twyla Tharp’s virtuosity, and Lucinda Childs's genius. Morris was flat broke but found a group of likeminded artists that danced together, travelled together, slept together. No one wanted to break the spell or miss a thing, because “if you missed anything, you missed everything .” This collective, led by Morris’s fiercely original vision, became the famed Mark Morris Dance Group. Suddenly, Morris was making a fast ascent. Celebrated by The New Yorker ’s critic as one of the great young talents, an androgynous beauty in the vein of Michelangelo’s David, he and his company had arrived. Collaborations with the likes of Mikhail Baryshnikov, Yo-Yo Ma, Lou Harrison, and Howard Hodgkin followed. And so did controversy: from the circus of his tenure at La Monnaie in Belgium to his work on the biggest flop in Broadway history. title: Out Loud (The Pair Book 3)
description: He has said it in Afrikaans, in the dark, with his hand over Theo's mouth. He has never once said it in English. Wessel Marais has a country again, and a seat in a boat, and a man who has waited three years for him to say one true thing out loud in a room where somebody could hear it. What he does not have is a father who will use his name. Theo Rooke came out on live television at twenty-one and has been the brave one ever since. He has one rule, made in a car park in Ely with his hands shaking — never a closeted man, never again — and he is about to discover that it was never about Wes, and never about the man he made it about either, and that he has spent three years quietly charging an innocent man interest on somebody else's debt. They are the fastest pair in the world and they are still lying to each other. One of them has a letter he will not open. One of them has a name he has not said out loud in seven years. And a journalist has a date — the twelfth of September — which only three people could have given him. It is going to turn out to be somebody they both love. Six minutes on a Sunday in August will decide what the last three years were for, and it will not go the way either of them has planned, and afterwards there will still be a kitchen to buy a pan for. Two men. One boat. Forty centimetres. And nowhere left to hide. Second-chance · coming out · found family · forced proximity · one couple across all three books · explicit The trilogy's hard-won, imperfect HEA lands here.  if(window.mix_csa){window.mix_csa('[cel_widget_id="tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_2"]', '#CardInstanceI2WKA7TAgpSSpHPZDWnVvw')('mark', 'bb')} if(window.uet){window.uet('bb','tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_2',{wb: 1})} ._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_icon_core_report__Fs1ah{color

title: Count Out Loud
description: A disciplined trainer builds a precise system of commands and accountability that quickly moves beyond the gym floor. Briony Catt uses measured counts and steady authority to guide both her husband and a new client through increasingly intense sessions. What begins as structured physical work becomes a private arrangement where obedience, observation, and carefully chosen words carry heavy emotional weight. Graham, accustomed to being useful, finds himself repositioned as witness and metronome while Odette, seeking structure, discovers how quickly professional boundaries can shift under a commanding voice. The three negotiate clear terms and a stop signal, yet the real tension lies in what each is willing to reveal, repeat, and endure once the counting begins. Briony’s methods expose pride, desire, and the need to be seen in new roles. Graham must learn to speak only what he is told while Odette learns to receive praise and correction without flinching. Every rep and every number tightens the dynamic between them, turning routine training into a test of how far they will let the cadence strip away their usual defenses. The story follows the slow tightening of this arrangement, the small failures that cost privileges, and the growing hunger for the next command. It explores the private language of control and the way three people learn to hold one another in place through nothing more than breath, numbers, and the refusal to look away.  if(window.mix_csa){window.mix_csa('[cel_widget_id="tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_3"]', '#CardInstanceETwKlcv63JUjzWzXEHKs6w')('mark', 'bb')} if(window.uet){window.uet('bb','tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_3',{wb: 1})} ._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_icon_core_report__Fs1ah{color:#0f1111;color:var(--aok-sfs-color-page-primary-norma

title: Out Loud
description: Thrust into the country environs of the Pacific Northwest, Klein, a precocious, yet introverted fourteen-year-old, is confronted with her abusive past for the first time when a repressed memory emerges. Shaken, she realizes she can no longer hide from her secret. Klein becomes perversely drawn to a classmate and neighbor, Ed Boons, after discovering they have a shared bond. They form an odd alliance, but life becomes increasingly complicated as Klein learns more about Ed’s escalating abusive family life and the subsequent CPS investigation of his home. Klein wants nothing more than to be transported from her haunting memories—to be unfettered, and normal again. Yet, the more embroiled she becomes in Ed’s life, the more she’s forced to grapple with her own past. As she navigates through distracted parents, isolation, and bullies, a semblance of clarity surfaces and an unformed, subconscious idea arises: Can she save herself by saving Ed first?  if(window.mix_csa){window.mix_csa('[cel_widget_id="tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_8"]', '#CardInstanceEOhZk4o1OU_sY8RMbnAkgA')('mark', 'bb')} if(window.uet){window.uet('bb','tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_8',{wb: 1})} ._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_icon_core_report__Fs1ah{color:#0f1111;color:var(--aok-sfs-color-page-primary-normal-fg,#0f1111);display:inline-block;-webkit-filter:none;filter:none;-webkit-filter:var(--aok-sfs-effect-mode-dark-color-silhouette-white,none);filter:var(--aok-sfs-effect-mode-dark-color-silhouette-white,none);height:20px;margin-right:4px;width:20px}._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_modal_spinner__3bz5K,._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_popover_inner__3tPIV{padding:20px 24px 0;width:65vw}._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_modal_spinner__3bz5K{height:15vh;margin-top:10vh;text-align:

title: Out Loud: 30 days to a braver English voice
description: Do you understand English perfectly but freeze when it's time to speak? Speak English More Confidently: A 30-Day Practice Guide is a simple, step-by-step plan for learners who know the words but struggle to say them out loud. In just 10-15 minutes a day, you'll move from quiet practice on your own to real conversations, interviews, and a two-minute speech you can be proud of. Inside, you'll find easy daily tasks, calming techniques for nerves, useful phrases for getting unstuck, and a printable progress tracker. No perfect grammar needed, just a willingness to start. Your English is already better than you think.
